hits.snippet: View organization page for UASFeed 30 followers Archer Aviation just agreed to acquire Boeing's Insitu, Wisk Aero, and SkyGrid - a single deal that pulls fixed-wing tactical UAS, autonomous eVTOL, and airspace-management software under one roof. That's a genuinely broad bet: Archer started as an eVTOL air-taxi company, and this move signals they see the real opportunity in owning the full autonomy/airspace stack rather than just building one aircraft type. Worth watching how the integration goes - Insitu's tactical ISR heritage, Wisk's autonomous passenger ambitions, and SkyGrid's traffic-management software are three genuinely different product cultures to merge into one company. Full details on the acquisition below. [...] Archer Aviation has agreed to acquire three Boeing subsidiaries, Wisk Aero, Insitu, and SkyGrid, in a deal that combines autonomous eVTOL aircraft, uncrewed systems, and airspace management technology with Archer's aviation AI platform, creating what the companies describe as an end-to-end physical AI platform spanning commercial aerospace, defense, and air traffic management. hits.snippet: 44,095 followers Archer Aviation has agreed to acquire former rival Wisk Aero from Boeing, along with SkyGrid and Insitu Inc, in a deal that will give Boeing about a 16.5% stake in Archer after closing. The acquisition follows a 2021 trade-secret lawsuit between Archer and Wisk that was settled in 2023 and led to a collaboration on autonomous technology; Archer has also raised $430 million for its defense business and another $300 million from institutional investors including BlackRock and Wellington in 2025. hits.snippet: August 11, 2026 - The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries. The deal will combine complementary capabilities developed over decades in autonomy, electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) – creating a groundbreaking end-to-end physical AI platform for aerospace and defense. [...] Archer’s Founder and CEO, Adam Goldstein said, “This is a watershed moment for Archer and the future of physical AI in aerospace and defense. hits.snippet: Today, we signed definitive agreements to acquire @Wisk.aero, @Skygridai, and @Insitu\_inc from @Boeing, with Boeing taking a stake in Archer and becoming a strategic partner. We anticipate closing the transaction by year end. Wisk will accelerate our Halo/Thunder dual-use aircraft platform. Deploying nascent tech early in defense benefits our entire business. Wisk has some of the most advanced autonomy, flight controls, and sensor technologies in the industry. We plan to deploy that technology on Halo first, so that we can harden it and then bring it back to the air taxi platform when the FAA is ready to certify autonomy for passenger air taxis.
